name: Magnesium Deficiency
description: Magnesium is the central atom of the chlorophyll molecule and essential for photosynthesis. Deficiency causes characteristic interveinal chlorosis on older leaves, commonly seen in acidic, leached tropical soils.
symptoms: Yellow interveinal chlorosis on older leaves (green veins, yellow tissue between)
Leaf margins may remain green or turn purple in some crops
Reduced root development and storage organ size
causes: Acidic, sandy soils with low cation exchange capacity
Excessive potassium application competing with magnesium uptake
High rainfall leaching magnesium from soil
Acidic soil pH limiting magnesium availability
treatments: Apply dolomitic lime (calcium-magnesium carbonate) to acidic soils
Foliar spray of magnesium sulfate (Epsom salt) solution (2%)
Apply magnesium sulfate (kieserite) as soil application
Use potassium magnesium sulfate (K-Mag) for balanced supply
prevention: Maintain soil pH at 6.0-7.0 with dolomitic lime
Use balanced fertilization — avoid excessive potassium
Incorporate organic matter to improve nutrient retention
Include magnesium in regular fertilizer program
